'''Maria Heep-Altiner''' (born 29 December 1959 in [[Niederzeuzheim]]) is a German mathematician, actuary and university lecturer.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://eiopa.europa.eu/Publications/Administrative/26._Heep-Altiner__Maria.pdf|title=Maria Heep Altiner|last=|first=|date=|website=European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

== Life ==
After graduating from the Prince Johann Ludwig School &nbsp;in [[Hadamar]] in 1978, Heep-Altiner studied [[mathematics]] and [[economics]] at the [[University of Bonn]]. In 1989 she earned her doctorate in mathematics on the [[number theory]] topic "Period relations for <math>GL_2(f)</math>" under [[Günter Harder]] and [[Michael Rapoport]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=116247|title=Maria Heep – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=22 February 2019}}</ref>

She then worked as an [[actuary]] for [[Atradius|Gerling]],  before she moved companies in 1994 to Allgemeine Versicherungs-AG. There she became the actuarial manager for property insurance. In 2006, she moved to [[Talanx]], where she was responsible for setting up an internal holding model.<ref name=":0" />

In 2008, Heep-Altiner returned to academia as a professor at the Institute of Insurance at [[Cologne university of applied sciences]].<ref name="TH Köln 2020">{{cite web | title=Personendetailseite | website=TH Köln | date=20 January 2020 | url=https://www.th-koeln.de/personen/maria.heep-altiner/ | language=de | access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref> There she is responsible for the area of finance in the insurance company.

She is a member of the [[German Actuarial Society]] executive board.

In addition, she has co-published various publications on various actuarial topics, in particular on the [[Solvency II Directive 2009]].
